kept.title: start_ox_worker says workers inherit the lead's mode, but with no session host a worker starts read-only
kept.experience: The description (and the server instruction at src/workers.rs:826) says workers inherit the parent's permission mode. Without a running OX session host, jobs.rs maps inherit to workspace_write.unwrap_or(false) (src/workers/jobs.rs:327-337, comment at 327 says 'starts read workers by default'). A lead agent that expects an editing worker gets a read-only one and only finds out from the result. docs/configuration.md states this correctly, but the tool text the lead actually reads does not.
kept.fix: Append to the start_ox_worker description: 'With no OX session host running, inherit means read-only; pass permission_mode "write" when the worker must edit files.' Same sentence for the server instructions at src/workers.rs:826.

kept.title: mode enum and task limits are undocumented: session is never described, and goal and workflow constraints are hidden
kept.experience: The mode enum is [session, goal, workflow] with no description. The tool description only says 'goal for Codex Goal mode or workflow for a Claude Code workflow', so the lead cannot tell what session is. The real constraints are enforced only at call time (jobs.rs:350-358): goal needs runtime codex and an objective of at most 4000 characters, workflow needs runtime claude, and jobs.rs:619 fails the job if Claude never calls its Workflow tool. The phrase 'stock-client coding session' at src/workers.rs:862 is also unclear to a lead agent.
kept.fix: Give mode a description: 'session: plain background coding session on either runtime. goal: Codex only; the task becomes the Codex goal objective, max 4000 characters. workflow: Claude Code only; the job fails if the Workflow tool is not used.' Replace 'stock-client coding session' with 'background Codex or Claude Code session in this project'.

kept.title: list_ox_models gives no metadata to choose a model, and its output fields and paging are undocumented
kept.experience: Each row carries only model, provider, auth, starred (src/workers.rs:712-716). The catalog already has per-alias context_window, which main.rs:874 model_contexts() computes and only desktop_settings.rs:142 reads. The description says 'unless the task needs another model' but gives the lead nothing to judge that by. The response also has worker_available, account, main_client and next_offset (lines 730-747) that the description never explains. It does not say that next_offset means more pages exist, and PAGE_SIZE is 40 (line 32), so a lead can miss models.
kept.fix: Add context_window (null when unknown) to each model row from model_contexts(). Document the output in the description: 'Each row has context_window when known. worker_available: true means the route can run start_ox_worker. A non-null next_offset means more models; pass it as offset.' Leave out price tiers or reasoning flags unless the catalog stores them; I found no such fields.

kept.title: delegate_to_ox_model omits its 90-second timeout and 96 KiB task limit
kept.experience: WORKER_TIMEOUT is 90 seconds (line 33, applied at line 776), and the task limit is 96 KiB (line 754). Neither appears in the tool description or the task schema. A lead that sends a long or multi-step task gets a timeout after 90 seconds, or a size error, and has no way to know ahead of time. docs/configuration.md states the 90-second limit, but the tool text does not.
kept.fix: Change the description to: 'Send one independent text request to the named API model. It times out after 90 seconds and takes a task of up to 96 KiB. For multi-step work with files or a shell, use start_ox_worker instead.' Put the same limit on the task property.

kept.title: permission_mode comment promises native preset names, but the schema enum rejects them
kept.experience: The comment on Start.permission_mode says the value can be 'a native preset name'. permission_level (jobs.rs:46-62) accepts plan, default, accept_edits and bypass_permissions. But the MCP schema at src/workers.rs:870 accepts only inherit, read, write, classifier and yolo, so an MCP client never sends those names. The code and the advertised contract disagree.
kept.fix: Either delete 'or a native preset name' from the comment at jobs.rs:40, or drop the unused aliases from permission_level so the code matches the schema.

kept.title: Composer Model picker cannot select a subscription route
kept.experience: The Model chip opens a picker built only from catalog aliases (model_entries, route_chip.rs:29-41). choices() returns nothing for Kind::Model (route_chip.rs:44). A user on an OX API alias cannot switch back to ChatGPT or Claude subscription from the composer; subscription routes are only reachable through the header route picker, which the composer chip does not mention.
kept.fix: Prepend a subscription row to the Model picker: an Entry with id "" and label "<runtime> subscription" (ChatGPT / Claude), and have choose_model map an empty id to runtime.route(None) (the same path as the subscription button in worker_sheet.rs:402-411). Skip the row when the session already runs that subscription.

kept.title: Choosing a model in the Model picker silently opens a new session
kept.experience: choose_model (route_chip.rs:75-93) emits NewModelRoute for any alias on a different route, and host.rs:526-533 immediately opens that route and a NewDraft. The picker row (model_picker.rs:302-309) shows only the alias label. Only the Effort/Speed rows (choice_row, route_chip.rs:115-119) prefix 'New session ·', and the Model kind never reaches choice_row because choices() returns empty for it. The user can lose the context of the current session without warning.
kept.fix: Compute the same new-route flag for ModelPicker rows (e.g. pass a `starts_new_session: bool` per Entry from model_entries using store.same_model_route) and render the 'New session' suffix in model_picker.rs row() around line 302-309, or show a footer line in the picker when the highlighted row starts a new session.

kept.title: Model chip shows the window route, not the selected session's route
kept.experience: Billing is read from store.profile().route (route_chip.rs:207), but a subscription session with no model shows self.route.label() (route_chip.rs:208), and self.route is the workbench's window route (workbench.rs:80). A ChatGPT session opened while the window is on Claude shows 'Claude subscription' in the Model chip. worker_sheet.rs:37-47 already states the session's route must be used, not the window's.
kept.fix: Replace self.route.label() with store.profile().route.label() on route_chip.rs:208 so the chip uses the same route as the billing match on line 207.

kept.title: API Model chip drops the runtime name
kept.experience: For Billing::Api the chip always reads 'OX API · <alias>' (route_chip.rs:212-219), whatever the runtime. Route::label (ox-desk-core runtime.rs:92-93) renders a Claude Code API route as 'Claude Code · OX API · <alias>'. In the composer, a Claude Code route and a Codex route on the same alias look identical, so the harness is not visible on the chip that matters most for picking one.
kept.fix: Prefix the API branch with store.profile().route.runtime.name() (for example format!("{} · OX API · {}", runtime.name(), model)), matching Route::label. Use the same wording in the subscription branch.

kept.title: Phone worker sheet offers an unlabeled 'Subscription (default)' even for Codex
kept.experience: fillWorkerModels always adds the option 'Subscription (default)' with value "" (app.js:1525). Switching the runtime select to Codex does not rebuild it (renderWorkerMode at app.js:1546-1571 only changes modes). The option does not say which account it bills (ChatGPT vs Claude). The desktop disables the subscription option for Codex workers (worker_sheet.rs:394-411, subscription_ok) and labels it via subscription_label (worker_sheet.rs:188-193). On the phone, a Codex worker with the subscription option is only refused by the host, and the notice then shows the host's text or the generic 'The host refused this worker.' (app.js:1606).
kept.fix: In fillWorkerModels, label the option with the runtime's account ('ChatGPT subscription' for codex, 'Claude subscription' for claude), and call fillWorkerModels from $("worker-runtime").onchange. For a worker on codex, disable the option and select the first starred model, mirroring worker_sheet.rs:394-411.

kept.title: Phone sheets do not start from the parent session's route; handoff runtime is flipped
kept.experience: The desktop sheets start from the selected session's route (worker_sheet.rs:37-47 Choice::new sets runtime and model from route.billing). The phone's start-worker handler (app.js:1573) and the worker form keep whatever the last choice was, so a worker started from a Claude-API session defaults to subscription. The phone handoff handler also flips the runtime to the other one (app.js:1427-1428), while the desktop keeps route.runtime, so the same action defaults differently on the two surfaces.
kept.fix: In start-worker.onclick and the handoff open path, set worker-runtime to selected.scope.route.runtime and the model select to selected.scope.route.billing.api (or '' for subscription), before calling fillWorkerModels. Make the handoff default match worker_sheet.rs Choice::new (same runtime, other route is a deliberate choice).

kept.title: Disabled Codex subscription button gives no reason
kept.experience: For a Codex worker, the subscription button is disabled (subscription_ok at worker_sheet.rs:395), and the model reads 'Choose a model…' (line 398). Nothing says Codex workers need an OX API model. The error appears only after Start worker, from worker_start's validation.
kept.fix: When subscription_ok is false, add small(p, "Codex workers need an OX API model.") under the Model row in model_row (worker_sheet.rs:391-420). Optionally pre-select the first starred model.

kept.title: Phone mode choices have no explanation
kept.experience: The phone labels modes 'Codex goal' and 'Claude workflow' (app.js:1541-1545) with no description. The desktop shows a one-line note per mode (worker_sheet.rs:173-180 mode_note, rendered at line 481: 'Codex keeps working toward the task as an objective.' and 'Claude Code runs the task with its Workflow tool.'). Goal and Workflow are the least obvious terms in the sheet.
kept.fix: Add a small text element under worker-mode-group in app.js, and set it from a map with the same strings as worker_sheet.rs mode_note, updated in renderWorkerMode.

kept.title: Blank Claude draft process is spawned at startup but never listed in Running, footer, or ox ps
kept.experience: Opening the desktop starts a Claude process for the empty draft (open_claude at store/claude.rs:384-389, prepare_claude_draft at :275-281). It is invisible: claude_live() excludes the blank owner (:748), so host processes() (ox-host/src/engine.rs:1996-1997, 'if threads.is_empty() continue') skips it. The user sees a Claude process burning resources with no row, no count, and no End button, which matches the 6 s opus process in the dogfood screenshot.
kept.fix: Either start the blank draft lazily (only when the user focuses the composer or types), or include it in processes() as kind 'draft' with running=false and a label like 'Draft, not started'. Also make the draft's model/route match the selected route before spawning, and add the draft to ox ps output so it is consistent with the panel.

kept.title: Footer and panel header use different counts for RUNNING
kept.experience: The panel header shows RUNNING · {processes.len()} (all live rows, including idle ones, running.rs:248 and :378), while the sidebar footer shows running_count(), which counts only busy rows (running.rs:113, used at views/host.rs:1066 and :1412). With one idle Claude process the panel says RUNNING · 1 and the footer says RUNNING · 0, exactly as in the dogfood screenshot.
kept.fix: Use one helper for both places, e.g. fn summary(&self) -> String returning 'RUNNING · {busy}' plus ' · {idle} idle' when idle > 0. Call it from running.rs:378 and host.rs:1412, and drop the separate count in host.rs:1066 so they cannot diverge.

kept.title: Title-generation processes are invisible and can bill API tokens
kept.experience: generate_impl spawns a separate 'ox claude' or 'ox codex' child (inference.rs:45-48, with --model alias for API billing, line 55) for every new conversation title. It is not in the host's self.running, so it never appears in the Running panel, the footer, or ox ps. Each run can take up to 30 s (line 154) and costs API tokens with no visible indication.
kept.fix: Route title jobs through the host as kind 'title' processes with running=true while in flight, so they appear in the panel and ox ps. At minimum, add a 'Titles: N generating' line in the panel footer and a one-line note in the README about the cost of automatic titles and how to disable them.

kept.title: Worker rows do not show their parent session
kept.experience: ProcessView (host_protocol.rs:164-179) has no parent field, so a worker row only says 'Worker · <project> · up Xm' (running.rs:290-300). The user cannot tell which conversation spawned it, and ending it does not show what it belongs to. The engine already knows the owner via self.workers.get(scope, t) (ox-host/src/engine.rs:2003-2006), but does not send it.
kept.fix: Add 'parent: Option<String>' (the owning thread's title or id) to ProcessView. Fill it in engine.rs processes() from the worker record, and in running.rs:290 render it as 'Worker of <parent-title>' in place of the generic kind_label. Mirror the field in ox ps (src/ps.rs Row) as a 'PARENT' column.

kept.title: Idle reaper is not explained in the Running panel
kept.experience: Idle processes are ended after 30 minutes by default (DEFAULT_IDLE_MINUTES = 30, ox-host/src/engine.rs:259, override OX_HOST_IDLE_MINUTES) but the panel only shows 'idle 12m' (running.rs:40) and an 'End all idle' button. Nothing says a process will end on its own, when, or that sessions stay resumable (engine.rs:2148 doc). The user may be surprised when a process disappears.
kept.fix: Expose the timeout in the host hello or ProcessView (for example 'reap_after_secs'). Then change idle_label at running.rs:40 to 'idle 12m · auto-end in 18m' when the timeout is nonzero, and add a tooltip or small line under the header: 'Idle sessions end after 30 min and can be resumed.'

kept.title: Wrong-billing error shown as 'Sign in to Claude'
kept.experience: On the subscription route, if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is set in the environment, verify_initialization (line 286) returns PermissionDenied 'Claude Code reported a different billing route'. Line 145 maps every PermissionDenied on a subscription route to Event::SignInRequired, so the status line (workbench.rs:599, 607) says 'Sign in to Claude'. Signing in does not fix an env var, so the user is sent to the wrong fix.
kept.fix: Give the billing mismatch its own error kind or Event (for example Event::BillingMismatch) and stop mapping it to SignInRequired at line 145. Map only the no-subscription case (subscription_type empty, token_source None) to SignInRequired. For the mismatch, return Closed with a message that names the source reported in caps.account.api_key_source or token_source, for example 'Claude Code is using ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from your environment. Unset it, or choose the API route.'

kept.title: Discovery error sticks in the banner and duplicates the status line
kept.experience: A failed discovery sets s.message to the raw error (for example '<path> must be a private directory owned by the current account'). Nothing clears it on a later successful discovery; only the banner's Dismiss (host.rs:1429) does. The same text also reaches the pane status via launch_error (workbench.rs:600-611), so the user sees it twice, and the banner outlives the fault after a host restart.
kept.fix: Store discovery failures in a separate field, for example s.discovery.error. Clear it in the Ok branch (discovery.rs around line 329). Render it in the banner only when the pane status does not already show the same text, so the message appears once.

kept.title: Permission-directory error loops on Reconnect
kept.experience: private_directory returns the raw 'must be a private directory owned by the current account' error. The only action offered is the full-width Reconnect button (workbench.rs:770). Reconnect runs ensure_running, which calls prepare again, so it fails the same way every time. The user is not told which path to fix or how.
kept.fix: When the directory is a real directory (not a symlink) owned by uid(), tighten it with set_permissions(0o700) and re-check, so the fault repairs itself. If the owner is wrong, or the repair fails, return a message that names the fix: 'OX state directory <path> must be mode 700 and owned by you. Run: chmod 700 <path>'. Do not offer Reconnect for this error; for example, retry_once (workbench.rs:255-258) should skip it.

kept.title: Alias-mismatch error tells the user to confirm, but no confirm control appears
kept.experience: Resuming a session whose bound API alias differs from the route returns 'Confirm the original OX API alias before resuming this session'. That text goes through Data::Failed into claude_closed, which sets Connection::Closed and shows Reconnect. Reconnect does not change the alias, so the user is stuck. The alias chooser that would fix this (host.rs:1313 'Choose the billing alias to resume') is only reached when route is None (host.rs:747-750).
kept.fix: Return a typed error for this case and, when the sidebar receives it, set choose_route = Some((project, row)) so the 'Choose the billing alias to resume' picker opens. Do not show Reconnect for this error. If the picker is not wanted, at least replace the text with the action: 'Choose the saved alias in the sidebar to resume this session'.

kept.title: Claude Code version-floor error offers a useless Reconnect and omits the found version
kept.experience: verify_initialization already parses the actual version (line 270, 'actual') but the message at lines 277-283 only states the floor and says 'Check claude --version'. The error becomes Closed(reason), so Reconnect is shown (workbench.rs:591-594, 770). Reconnect respawns the same old CLI and fails again.
kept.fix: Include the found version in the message, for example 'Claude Code 2.0.5 found; OX Desktop needs 2.1.0 or later. Update Claude Code, then press Reconnect.' Compute it from `actual`, which is already in scope. Keep Reconnect, since the user is expected to update first.

kept.title: Raw transport errors shown as the connection status
kept.experience: The status line shows Connection::Closed(reason) verbatim (workbench.rs:608). Reasons come from io errors, such as 'Session host disconnected' and 'Incomplete or oversized host frame' (host_client.rs:35-42), or 'Connection closed' and 'Claude Code closed its output' (process.rs:101-106). The user gets no hint about whether to restart the host, reinstall, or simply reconnect.
kept.fix: Map the reason by io::ErrorKind or a short enum to plain copy with one action. For example, UnexpectedEof becomes 'The session host stopped. Reconnect to start it.', and InvalidData becomes 'The session host sent an unreadable reply. Restart OX Desktop.' Keep the raw text only in the copy-message control and the log.

kept.title: API Claude thread with empty model list is a dead end
kept.experience: When the thread needs a Claude alias but self.models is empty, the sidebar skips the alias picker (condition at line 750 requires !self.models.is_empty()). It shows 'Configure the saved provider <provider> in Settings', which does not name the missing alias or offer a retry of model discovery.
kept.fix: When models is empty and row.needs_claude_alias(), show 'Discovering models… / Retry' that calls start_discovery or model discovery again, and keep the picker once models arrive. Do not send the user to Settings for an alias problem.

kept.title: Private-directory error exposes raw path and jargon, shown twice
kept.experience: The user sees '<full path> must be a private directory owned by the current account' in the header and again in the red banner, above a full-width Reconnect button that will fail the same way. 'Private directory' and 'current account' do not say what to change.
kept.fix: Change the format to: "OX can't use {path} because only you should be able to access it. Run chmod 700 {path} (or delete the folder so OX recreates it), then press Reconnect." Show this message in one place only (the banner) and drop the duplicate header copy.

kept.title: API key file error gives no path and no fix command
kept.experience: The user gets 'ox-api-keys.json must be owned by the current user with mode 0600' with no folder and no command. The same text is reused at line 148 after a failed chmod, so a permissions failure looks like an ownership problem.
kept.fix: Return the full path and a fix: "Your API key file {path} must belong to your user and be readable only by you. Run chmod 600 {path} and try again." At line 148 use a separate message: "Could not set {path} to owner-only access ({err}). Run chmod 600 {path} yourself."

kept.title: 'different billing route' is internal jargon with no next step
kept.experience: A Claude session that starts under the wrong account shows 'Claude Code reported a different billing route'. 'Billing route' is an internal term and the user is not told which account to sign in to.
kept.fix: Use: "Claude Code is signed in to a different account than this route ({route label}). Sign in to the matching account with claude /login, or choose another route." Pass the expected route label into verify_initialization, which already has billing in scope.

kept.title: Unavailable-command error does not name the command or the route
kept.experience: Typing an unsupported slash command shows 'This command is unavailable on this route.' The user cannot tell which command failed or which route is meant, and no next step is given.
kept.fix: Take the command name from text (first word) and the route label from the session: format it as "/{name} is not available on {route label}. Type /status to see what this session supports."

kept.title: Lease wait messages use internal wording and give no time or next step
kept.experience: Resuming a thread can show 'Waiting for Codex to release the thread' or 'Waiting for Claude Code to release the session'. 'Release' and 'lease' are internal ideas. The user does not know whether to wait or act.
kept.fix: Use: "Codex is still closing its terminal for this thread. Wait a few seconds, then try again." and for line 419: "Claude Code is still finishing the previous turn for this session. Wait a few seconds, then try again."

kept.title: Handoff context-fit error uses 'minimum' and 'exchange' jargon
kept.experience: Long handoffs fail with 'The new request and the minimum earlier context (the first request and the latest exchange, about N tokens) do not fit...'. The user has to work out what is being measured and what to cut.
kept.fix: Use: "This request does not fit {model}'s {window}-token context, even with the first message and the latest reply kept (about {used} tokens). Shorten the request or choose a model with a larger context."

kept.title: Remote 'Allow terminal access' grants a host shell with no warning or confirm
kept.experience: In Remote access > Paired devices, each device gets a plain secondary button 'Allow terminal access' (also 'Run in OX terminal' at line 197). Clicking it immediately gives a paired phone or device a terminal on this computer. The button looks like any other settings toggle, and the only explanation is the phone-side how-to in desktop/ox-host-web/assets/settings.js:417. A new user does not learn what the grant means before clicking.
kept.fix: Keep the label but add a one-line consequence under the device row, for example 'Lets this device run commands as you on this computer.' Put the grant behind a confirm step (the phone already has one: settings.js confirmAction, lines 336-355, with a danger button). Use the danger style for 'Allow terminal access' and keep 'Disable terminal access' as the neutral action.

kept.title: Ending a busy session has three different names and an un-marked confirm
kept.experience: The desktop menu item is 'End session' (thread_menu.rs:202), the palette says 'End session' (palette.rs:360), the inline confirm says 'End running session' (thread_menu.rs:81), and the phone menu says 'Stop' (index.html:168, which triggers the turn-level stop). The confirm button is a primary (Save-styled) button (thread_menu.rs:89-96), not a danger button. It does not say that the running turn, approvals and workers will be cancelled, which the code comment at line 43-44 says happens.
kept.fix: Use 'End session' for process end everywhere. Rename the phone 'Stop' to 'Stop turn' so it is not confused with End. Change the confirm label to 'End session and cancel N running workers' or 'End session and cancel this turn', and render it with a danger style (add a danger variant to kit::button, which currently only has Primary/Secondary).

kept.title: Permission mode labels on the phone repeat internal names and hide their meaning
kept.experience: The phone worker and handoff mode pickers show 'Read (Read only · Plan)', 'Write (Workspace · Accept edits)', 'Classifier (Auto-review · Auto)' and 'YOLO (YOLO · bypass)' (index.html:259-263, and again at 288). These are internal mode names, and YOLO is repeated. The desktop uses 'YOLO · bypass permissions' (desk-core runtime.rs:162). The plain-language descriptions that already exist in runtime.rs:169-181 are not shown on the phone, so a new user cannot tell what YOLO does before selecting it.
kept.fix: Use one caption per mode: 'Read only', 'Workspace', 'Auto-review', 'YOLO', and show the existing runtime.rs description() text as the option's hint line or under the select when it changes. Drop the parenthesised duplicates. Keep the existing YOLO warning (worker-warning, app.js:1566-1569) and make it name the risk.

kept.title: Reasoning and token options show raw config values as buttons
kept.experience: In the provider editor, the choice buttons map only a few values to captions (forms.rs:303-307: responses, chat_completions, anthropic_messages, true, false). Everything else is shown raw: 'drop' and 'forward' under 'Reasoning effort' (forms.rs:80-82), 'max_tokens' and 'max_completion_tokens', 'off', 'adaptive', 'manual' under 'Thinking mode', and 'system' and 'developer' under 'Developer role'. The fields have no help text, so 'drop' or 'forward' tells the user nothing.
kept.fix: Add a caption arm for each value in the match at forms.rs:303-307, for example 'drop' => 'Drop (do not send)', 'forward' => 'Forward to provider', 'adaptive' => 'Adaptive', 'manual' => 'Manual budget'. Add a short hint string to each field spec in the Spec table (forms.rs:33-110) and render it under the label. Make the same change in the phone table at desktop/ox-host-web/assets/settings.js:22 and :28.

kept.title: Send-message and theme choices are unclear for new users
kept.experience: The 'Send messages' row offers 'Ctrl / Cmd + Enter' and 'Enter' (behavior.rs:78-91). It does not say which one sends by default or what Shift+Enter does. The theme row offers 'System (Omarchy)' (behavior.rs:101), which assumes the user knows Omarchy. The first-run default is Enter sends (see the test at behavior.rs:168).
kept.fix: Change the captions to 'Enter sends · Shift+Enter for newline' and 'Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends · Enter for newline', and mark the default with 'Default'. Change 'System (Omarchy)' to 'Follow system' and show 'Omarchy' only when that theme is detected.

kept.title: Settings page names differ between desktop and phone
kept.experience: The desktop tabs (preferences.rs:1105-1113) are 'Providers', 'Starred models', 'Appearance & input', 'Legacy', 'Advanced'. The phone menu (desktop/ox-host-web/assets/settings.js:364-378) uses 'Providers & models', 'Favorites', 'Phone appearance & input' / 'Desktop appearance & input', 'Legacy Codex provider', 'Advanced configuration', and 'Install & notifications', which the desktop does not have as a tab. Someone who uses both sees different names for the same page. 'Accounts' and 'Credentials' also sit next to each other without saying that Credentials means API keys.
kept.fix: Use one name table for both clients: 'Accounts', 'Providers & models', 'API keys' (replacing 'Credentials' in both places), 'Starred models', 'Web search', 'Advanced configuration', and 'Legacy Codex provider' (shown only when present). Change preferences.rs:1105-1113 and settings.js:364-378 to match, and make the phone's 'Appearance & input' entries share one name with a device suffix.

kept.title: Idle-session reaper and sandbox status have no settings UI
kept.experience: The idle reaper (default 30 min, off with 0) is set only by the OX_HOST_IDLE_MINUTES environment variable (docs/design/threads-plan.md:132). A user who wants it shorter or off cannot find it in Settings on desktop or phone. Write workers now need bwrap and socat for their sandbox, and without them they fall back to edits only (docs/design/threads-plan.md:135). Nothing in Settings shows whether that sandbox is available, so a user can think a write worker is sandboxed when it is not.
kept.fix: Add an 'Idle sessions end after' choice (30 min default, 1 h, Never) to the end of behavior_page in behavior.rs, saved through the same host settings path as the other choices, and mirror it in settings.js. Add a read-only row under Accounts (preferences.rs, the Accounts card area around line 527) reading 'Worker sandbox: ready' or 'Worker sandbox: needs bwrap and socat, so workers can only edit files', which uses the existing host check.

kept.title: Footer RUNNING count disagrees with the panel above it
kept.experience: The RUNNING section header (running.rs:378) uses processes.len(), which includes idle processes, while the footer at host.rs:1412 uses running_count() (running.rs:113), which counts only busy ones. The same sidebar shows 'RUNNING · 1' above and 'RUNNING · 0' below, as in the dogfood screenshot.
kept.fix: Add a process_count() that returns self.processes.len() to Running, and use it in the footer: .child(small(p, format!("RUNNING · {}", self.running.read(cx).process_count()))). If the busy number matters, label it differently, e.g. 'BUSY · n', so the two labels cannot share a name.

kept.title: Footer row cannot shrink or wrap at sidebar widths
kept.experience: The footer is a non-wrapping row holding 'Back to thread' or 'Settings', the RUNNING label and a status dot, with justify_between. At the 190-256 px sidebar width used in tiling, the button and label have no flex_wrap or min_w_0 and can overflow or clip the sidebar edge.
kept.fix: Add .flex_wrap() to the outer footer row at host.rs:1389 (with .gap_y) and .min_w_0() plus .truncate() on the inner status row at host.rs:1404, so the count drops under the button instead of overflowing.

kept.title: Filter chips wrap to two lines in the sidebar
kept.experience: The chip row is row().gap_1().px_2().flex_wrap() for 'Running', 'Needs you' and 'Finished'. Their combined width is more than the usable ~240 px inside the 256 px sidebar, so the chips split across two lines, which looks broken and takes vertical space in a short tile.
kept.fix: Use .flex_nowrap() instead of .flex_wrap() at host.rs:636, give each chip .flex_1().min_w_0() (passed through kit::button or wrapped in a div), and let the label truncate. Alternatively shorten the labels to 'Run', 'Waiting', 'Done' only for the compact sidebar width.

kept.title: Window size fallback discards valid width or height
kept.experience: window_size() falls back to 1130x760 when either axis is small. A saved short tile such as 1000x400 (height < 480) loses its valid width too, so the window reopens at a size the user did not choose in a tiling WM.
kept.fix: Clamp each axis separately: size(px(self.width.max(360).min(10000) as f32), px(self.height.max(480).min(10000) as f32)), and keep the 1130x760 fallback only when width or height is 0 (never saved).

kept.title: Connection error shown twice in the header
kept.experience: The launch or connection error is shown as the status line under the thread title (status at workbench.rs:600) and again in the host-error banner (host.rs:1401-1411). In a narrow pane the same raw message wraps across both places and pushes the Reconnect control into the header.
kept.fix: Render the status line only when there is no banner: in workbench.rs, skip the status row when status equals the host message, or drop the banner for messages already shown in the header. Keep one place for the error, and keep Reconnect in the header row at workbench.rs:770-778 with .flex_none().

kept.title: No empty state when no thread is selected
kept.experience: With no selected thread the main column still renders the header, composer and controls, with nothing explaining the empty area. A grep for empty or no-selection copy in workbench.rs and host.rs finds nothing.
kept.fix: Before the header and composer are built (around workbench.rs:652-676), branch on whether a thread is selected. When none is, render a centred col().flex_1().items_center().justify_center() with small(p, "Pick a thread or start a new session") and a button that calls DeskAction::NewDraft, reusing the existing button helper.

kept.title: Phone shell summary keeps the closing quote
kept.experience: On the phone, a tool row for a wrapped shell command such as /bin/bash -lc "git status" shows the title `git status"` with a stray trailing quote (same for single quotes). The regex strips only the opening quote. The desktop shell_summary in cards.rs:122-142 strips both quotes, so the two surfaces disagree.
kept.fix: After the existing replace, also strip one matching trailing quote, e.g. .replace(/^(?:\S*\/)?(?:bash|zsh|sh)\s+-[a-z]*c\s+['"]?/i, "").replace(/['"]$/, "") before .slice(0, 120). Add a case for `bash -lc "ls"` in the phone tests if they exist.

kept.title: Phone file-change rows show no paths and dump raw JSON
kept.experience: Every file-change tool row on the phone is titled "File changes" with no file names or counts. Expanding it shows JSON.stringify(data) (line 887), so each diff appears as one line with literal \n escapes instead of readable patch text. Users cannot tell which file changed without expanding and decoding JSON.
kept.fix:
In toolInfo, add a FileChange title from data.changes: one change gives its path, several give "N changed files". In toolText, for kind FileChange, return data.changes.map(c => c.path + "
" + c.diff).join("

") (the same layout desktop write_detail uses in cards.rs:263-270), instead of the JSON.stringify fallback.

kept.title: Desktop file-change summary has no diff stats
kept.experience: The collapsed header for a file change shows only the path or "N changed files" (cards.rs:147-150). Users cannot see how big a change is (+/- lines) before expanding, even though each FileChange carries the full diff text.
kept.fix: Count lines in c.diff: starts_with('+') and not starts_with("+++") for additions, starts_with('-') and not starts_with("---") for deletions. Sum across changes and render e.g. "src/a.rs · +12 −3" or "3 files · +40 −7". Keep compact() on the path. Apply the same counts to the phone title in app.js toolInfo.

kept.title: Diff output is unstyled and unwrapped in the desktop detail view
kept.experience: Tool details, including file diffs, render as one plain mono text node in a 190 px scroll box with whitespace_nowrap (cards.rs:397-405). Added and removed lines look the same, and long lines run off to the side. Reviewing a diff in the transcript is hard.
kept.fix: In detail(), when the item is FileChange, split the output into lines and render each as its own child div in a column. Give lines starting with '+' p.success text color and lines starting with '-' p.error. Keep the single-div path for other tools. The Palette already has success and error (used in transcript.rs:674 and :691).

kept.title: Preview keeps only the first 40 lines of output
kept.experience: Long command output shows only its first 40 lines or 6 KB, then says "Preview truncated. Copy for the full output." (cards.rs:407-415). The end of the output, where errors, exit summaries and test totals usually are, is hidden unless the user copies everything. The phone has no cap at all (app.js toolText) and puts the full output in a pre.
kept.fix: Keep a head and a tail in the preview. Build the text with full_text(entry), keep the first 20 and last 20 lines, and insert a line such as "… N lines hidden …" between them. The Copy button still copies everything. Update the cards.rs test at line 458 to check both ends.

kept.title: Find-in-transcript scans and lowercases all output on every keystroke
kept.experience: Each keystroke in the find box (InputEvent::Change at tools.rs:126) runs matches() on the UI thread. For every loaded tool item it builds the full text through cards::full_text, which copies the whole command output, then calls to_lowercase(). In long sessions with large outputs, typing lags.
kept.fix: Debounce the Change event with a short timer (about 150 ms, the same pattern the phone uses in composer-tools.js:308), or cache the lowercased text per ItemKey and revision. The cache also avoids repeated full_text copies while typing.

kept.title: Copy-the-line helper adds a false ellipsis for trailing newlines
kept.experience: A command or summary that ends with a newline, such as "git status\n", is shown as "git status…" in the header. compact() appends the ellipsis whenever the result is shorter than the input, and a trailing newline also makes it shorter.
kept.fix: Trim trailing whitespace before compact() (value.trim_end()), or only append the ellipsis when the cut happened before a non-whitespace character. Add "git status\n" to the test at cards.rs:436.

kept.title: Phone filter chips use different names and semantics than desktop
kept.experience: Desktop filters are Running / Needs you / Finished (host.rs:631-633). The phone shows All / Active / Requests / Finished. 'Active' is computed from capabilities (app.js:670-671: stop or steer) while desktop 'Running' is status === running (discovery.rs:549). A session can be 'Active' on the phone and absent from the desktop Running filter, and the same user sees two vocabularies for one state.
kept.fix: Rename the phone chips to Running / Needs you / Finished (data-filter values can stay). Change app.js:670-671 to filter on session.status === "running", matching discovery.rs:549, and the empty-state copy at app.js:745-748 to match.

kept.title: Phone row status shows raw host status strings, not desktop labels
kept.experience: Session rows on the phone print session.status verbatim (app.js:726), e.g. 'running', 'failed', 'interrupted' in lowercase monospace. Desktop maps the same values to 'Running', 'Error', 'Interrupted' (discovery.rs:221-229). The phone also says 'Needs input' (app.js:723) where desktop and the NEEDS YOU bar say 'Needs you'. The Running panel says 'Turn running' / 'Idle' (app.js:470) where desktop says 'Running'.
kept.fix: Port the discovery.rs status mapping into app.js (needs_input→'Needs you', running→'Running', failed→'Error', interrupted→'Interrupted', else empty), use 'Needs you' at app.js:723, and use 'Running' at app.js:470 for active processes.

kept.title: Phone approval has no terminal-review path while the turn is running
kept.experience: Desktop shows 'Decline and review in OX terminal…' on command approvals (ask_sheet.rs:225-245). The phone ask card (app.js ~770-830) renders only title, detail and choices. The only session-terminal entry, #operator-session, is hidden whenever caps includes 'stop' (app.js:1134-1139). projection.rs:167-168 adds 'stop' whenever the turn is running, which is exactly when an approval is pending. A phone user facing a shell-command approval has no session-scoped terminal path and cannot see what they are approving beyond the title.
kept.fix: Show the pending command in the phone ask card when the payload has it (check the wire ask shape). Show #operator-session when the session has a pending ask, even if 'stop' is present, so openPhoneTerminal('native-session', …) is reachable during approvals.

kept.title: Phone pairing copy names a menu path that does not exist on desktop
kept.experience: The pairing screen says 'Open Remote access in OX Desktop', but Remote access is a Preferences page (preferences.rs:1106) reached through the Settings button (host.rs:1403). The official Tailscale prompt in platform/remote.rs:424 uses the correct path, 'OX Desktop → Settings → Remote access', so the two surfaces disagree.
kept.fix: Change index.html:35 to 'Open Settings → Remote access in OX Desktop and scan a pairing code for your Tailscale account, or paste its pairing link below.'

kept.title: Push notification labels differ from desktop approval wording
kept.experience: A phone alert reads 'Approval needed' or 'Question waiting'. The desktop approval card header is 'NEEDS YOU · n' (ask_sheet.rs:18-23), the status is 'Needs you' (host.rs:706), and the phone's own bar is 'NEEDS YOU · n requests' (app.js:1175). The same event gets three phrasings.
kept.fix: Use the desktop vocabulary: approval → 'Needs you · approval', question → 'Needs you · question'. Keep the labels map in sw.js:66-69 as the single phone-side source.

kept.title: Needs-you blink from polish-plan 2.4 is not implemented
kept.experience: The status marker for a 'Needs you' row is a static p.warning color (kit/mod.rs:260). Nothing animates it, so a session waiting on the user looks the same as an idle one. Separately, workbench.rs:626 explicitly excludes Scene::Waiting from the activity runner, so the waiting state has no motion at all. polish-plan.md:89 specifies a 1 Hz two-frame blink on the 'Needs you' chip that stops after 10 s, and the grep for blink/sparkle across ox-desktop/src finds nothing.
kept.fix: Add a 1 Hz tick for rows whose status is 'Needs you' (kit/mod.rs row render), gated on Palette.motion && window.is_visible(), using the same cx.spawn + background_executor().timer pattern as activity.rs:63-75. Toggle the marker between p.warning and a dimmed variant, record a start Instant in the row or view state, and stop the timer after 10 s. The blink must not repaint the whole list: notify only the row entity.

kept.title: Running panel opens a new host socket and handshake every 5 s
kept.experience: While the sidebar panel is shown, the poll at running.rs:22 (POLL = 5 s) calls platform::list_processes() (running.rs:149). Each call runs connect_existing() (host_client.rs:61-70: Paths::discover, is_running, UnixStream::connect, Hello handshake) and then a ListProcesses round trip (host_client.rs:209-226). That is a full connection cycle every 5 s, even though the app already holds a live catalog subscription (host_client/catalog.rs watch_catalog). Running counts can disagree for up to 5 s, which is part of the RUNNING 1 vs 0 inconsistency in the dogfood shot.
kept.fix: Derive Running.processes and running_count() from the existing watch_catalog events (CatalogEvent::Replace/Update) instead of a second poller, keeping the poll only as a fallback when the catalog watch is down. As a smaller change, reuse one connection for the list request and drop the 5 s cadence to a longer idle interval when the window is not active.

kept.title: Synchronous stat and canonicalize inside UI-thread click handlers
kept.experience: The open-project path calls project.is_dir() directly on the UI thread (host.rs:742), and the recent-directory menu item calls directory.canonicalize() and project.is_dir() inside an on_click closure (host.rs:1187-1188). For a project on a stalled network mount or sshfs, these syscalls can freeze the window at click time, which feels like the app hung.
kept.fix: Move the filesystem checks into cx.background_spawn and apply the result with this.update(cx, ...) (host.rs:742 open path, host.rs:1187 menu click). Keep the 'Project unavailable' message as the result branch.

kept.title: Host ends busy sessions without the UI's busy confirmation
kept.experience: The busy confirmation lives only in the desktop UI (desktop/ox-desktop/src/views/workbench/thread_menu.rs:45-55, request_end). The host's end_thread (engine.rs:2053-2072) has no busy check. It calls store.end_session, which interrupts the running turn (compose.rs:467-500), then end_children cancels and ends running workers (engine.rs:2075). The web bridge accepts Action::EndSession with only approval.is_none() (desktop/ox-host-web/src/bridge.rs:235-236). A stale window, a web or remote client, or a repeated request can therefore kill a running turn and its workers with no prompt.
kept.fix: Add a `confirmed: bool` field to Action::EndSession (desktop/ox-desk-core/src/actions.rs:80). In end_thread, when thread_busy(thread) or any running worker exists and confirmed is false, return Err("This thread is busy. Confirm ending it, which cancels its running work."). The UI sets confirmed=true from its existing request_end confirmation path. Add a unit test next to the existing EndSession tests at engine.rs:3929.

kept.title: No cost or runtime cap on background worker runs
kept.experience: Each worker is spawned with tokio::spawn (jobs.rs:246) and no overall deadline. The Claude command (jobs.rs:425-441) passes no --max-turns or --max-budget-usd, and Workflow-mode workers (jobs.rs:421) may fan out subagents. Up to 4 workers (MAX_RUNNING, jobs.rs:18) can run indefinitely on a metered API route, and a stuck or looping worker holds its slot until someone cancels it by hand. Only the 90 s WORKER_TIMEOUT in src/workers.rs:776 bounds the MCP reply, not the worker itself.
kept.fix: Wrap the match in the spawned future (jobs.rs:247-251) with tokio::time::timeout(max_runtime, ...) and record an error "Worker stopped after N minutes". Default max_runtime to a conservative value, configurable in [workers]. For Claude, pass a per-worker budget flag, after confirming the exact name with `claude --help` on the installed version (e.g. --max-budget-usd or --max-turns), in the args block at jobs.rs:435.

kept.title: Write workers can run concurrently in the same project with no guard
kept.experience: The only admission check is the global slot count (jobs.rs:194-199, MAX_RUNNING=4). Nothing checks whether another running job already writes to the same cwd. Four write workers can therefore edit one checkout at once, each with acceptEdits or workspace-write, and can clobber each other's files. Parent and worker also share cwd (jobs.rs:401 current_dir(cwd)). A grep for worktree, writer and lock in src/ and desktop/ finds no per-project write guard.
kept.fix: In Jobs::start, before spawning, reject a write start when another non-finished job whose writes() is true has the same cwd, with "Another worker is already writing in this project. Wait for it or start a read worker." Store cwd on the entry. The stronger option is to run each write worker in its own `git worktree` under the OX state directory and merge it back on review. Start with the reject rule.

kept.title: YOLO grants never expire and outlive their session
kept.experience: set_grant (flows.rs:145-169) stores {scope, session} in ledger.data.grants with no timestamp or expiry. The grant keeps covering every future YOLO child of that session and its handoffs (yolo_grant, flows.rs:23-50). It survives end_session, host restarts and days of inactivity. The grant on a session that was ended still authorizes YOLO for later starts from it.
kept.fix: Store granted_at in Grant. In end_thread (engine.rs:2053) remove the grant for the ended thread when it is ended by the operator, or add a 24 h expiry check in yolo_grant (flows.rs:23) that ignores and prunes stale grants. Show the grant age in the YOLO sheet so the operator sees it.

kept.title: Project-wide YOLO default applies silently to every new session
kept.experience: yolo_grant falls back to the [workers] yolo_grant_projects list (flows.rs:44-50). A project listed there lets every future YOLO child start without the confirmation sheet. The operator may not remember the config entry, and a Codex or Claude start in that project becomes full-access with no prompt.
kept.fix: Keep the config default, but make the start path (flows.rs:324-333) return YoloAllowance::Grant{session: None} only with a visible badge in the launch sheet and in the session header ("YOLO by project default"). Also log one line per such start in the daemon log, so the default is auditable.

kept.title: Secrets shorter than four characters are not redacted
kept.experience: redact skips any configured secret under 4 bytes (upstream.rs:564, same rule at src/claude_gateway.rs:1027). A short key or token that reaches a task, worker transcript or error text is stored and shown unredacted. The risk is small because real keys are long, but the rule is silent.
kept.fix: Lower the threshold to 1 byte for exact-match of configured keys, or refuse to load a configured key shorter than 8 characters with a clear config error. Replace `secret.len() >= 4` in both places with a shared helper.

kept.title: Codex images and screenshots fail on Claude API routes
kept.experience: On a Codex session routed to an Anthropic-wire API alias, any input_image is rejected before the request leaves ox. User messages with a pasted screenshot hit line 665 ("has content type input_image, which this adapter slice does not support"). Tool results from view_image or screenshot tools hit line 743 ("is an image ... does not support in tool results"), so the whole turn fails. docs/compatibility.md:82 documents this as a gap, but Anthropic Messages accepts image blocks in both user content and tool_result content, so it is not a platform limit. This is likely the cause of the blocked screenshots.
kept.fix: In content_blocks (line 665) and tool_result_content (line 743), map input_image to an Anthropic image block. A data: URL becomes {"type":"image","source":{"type":"base64","media_type","data"}} and an https URL becomes {"type":"image","source":{"type":"url","url"}}. Inside tool_result, push the same block into the array. Keep input_file and audio rejected. Then update the module doc at lines 45-50 and docs/compatibility.md:82-84. Add a fixture test in tests/anthropic_adapter.rs.

kept.title: Handoff silently drops attachments and still says nothing was omitted
kept.experience: user_text (line 100-110) keeps only parts that have a text field. An image or file the user attached is dropped with no trace. A message that was only an attachment is removed by the empty-text filter at line 90, so it is not counted in total. The preamble built at line 443 then tells the target "Nothing was omitted." when the original conversation had images, so the agent does not know the screenshot existed.
kept.fix: In items(), count user parts without text and image-only messages, for example with an attachments counter stored in SelectionRefs. In preamble(), add a clause such as "N attachments from earlier messages were not carried." and stop saying "Nothing was omitted." when that count is nonzero. Mention the same in the handoff sheet notice in compose.rs.

kept.title: Read worker mode is dontAsk but docs and tool text say Claude Plan
kept.experience: Without a session host, a read worker on Claude Code is launched with --permission-mode dontAsk. The docs say read maps to Claude Plan: docs/configuration.md:756 and the start_ox_worker permission_mode description in src/workers.rs:870. The host path uses Level::preset (desktop/ox-desk-core/src/modes.rs:58, Plan). So the same level gets a different Claude mode depending on whether the host is running.
kept.fix: Either pass --permission-mode plan when !writes at jobs.rs:436 and confirm Plan works with --print and stream-json, or change the text at configuration.md:756 and workers.rs:870 to say read is dontAsk with read-only tools. Pick one and make the host and fallback paths match.

kept.title: Compatibility doc says Chat Completions rejects tool-result images, but code accepts them
kept.experience: docs/compatibility.md:83-84 says the Chat Completions adapter rejects images in tool results. src/adapters/chat_completions.rs:547-596 (tool_output) handles input_image and forwards it as a follow-up user message (line 386). The stale claim is repeated in the module comment of src/claude_request.rs:80-83. Readers are told to use the native route for something that already works.
kept.fix: Update docs/compatibility.md:82-85 to say Chat Completions maps user and tool-result images. Update the claude_request.rs module comment at lines 80-83 to match. Keep the Anthropic gap wording until finding 1 is fixed.

kept.title: Docs say workers start read without a host, but classifier and yolo are refused
kept.experience: docs/configuration.md:762-764 says that without a host, workers start with read access and write access when asked. src/workers/jobs.rs:340 returns an error for classifier and yolo when no host is running: "Classifier and YOLO workers need the OX session host". The tool call fails instead of starting a read worker, and the docs do not say so.
kept.fix: Add a sentence to configuration.md after line 764: without a host, classifier and yolo requests are refused and do not fall back to read.

kept.title: Handoff notice names an unqualified alias as an API provider
kept.experience: provider() at lines 545-560 takes the part before '/' as the vendor name. For an alias with no slash, such as "sonnet", the notice reads "sends the carried conversation to the sonnet API provider". That misstates the billing recipient on the one line meant to make it clear. Aliases are documented as qualified, so this should only appear for bad input.
kept.fix: In provider(), when alias has no '/', return "the API route for {alias}" instead of "the {alias} API provider". Add a test case next to provider_notices_name_the_receiving_provider at line 1145.
